records.shown:
Draft (215 of 400 words): We provide free after-school tutoring for students in grades 3–8 at two Bridgeport public schools. From October through May, groups of three students meet with a trained volunteer tutor twice a week for 90 minutes. We serve about 140 students each year, and the requested funding would support recruiting, training, and supporting 20 additional volunteer tutors and adding a third partner school, with the goal of serving 50 more students in the 2027–28 school year.

Our program director, a former Bridgeport teacher, leads the work with two site coordinators. Before tutoring, each volunteer completes eight hours of training in reading and math strategies and receives monthly coaching. In 2025–26, 58 tutors contributed about 4,100 hours, and 70% returned for a second year.

We measure student participation through attendance and academic progress through the district’s spring reading assessment. In 2025–26, 72% of students who attended at least 30 sessions gained one or more grade levels on that assessment. Students attended 81% of scheduled sessions on average.

Families take part through four Family Learning Nights each year, where they meet their child’s tutor and take home learning kits in English, Spanish, and Portuguese. About 30% of our students are multilingual learners, mostly from Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking families, so these materials help families engage with learning at home.
Review: The draft addresses all three requirements and describes the program’s schedule, staffing, progress measurement, and family participation. Clarify the assessment group size if available, and avoid presenting the learning kits’ effect as established without supporting evidence.
